newsitem.title: USA: Grove proposes becoming self-managed REIT.
newsitem.headline: Grove proposes becoming self-managed REIT.

text.p: Grove Real Estate Asset Trust said on Thursday it would propose becoming a self-administered and self-managed real estate investment trust, with control over properties in southern New England.
As part of this consolidation, Grove said it planned to raise up to $30 million in new equity and proposed changing its name to Grove Property Trust.
Grove, which filed preliminary proxy materials with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, said it sought shareholder approval to merge another 20 affiliated properties into its REIT structure.
These properties had been private partnerships, the company said.
Previously, Grove managed a portfolio of four properties with 257 apartments. If the proposal was approved, the REIT would manage 24 properties with 752 apartments, it said.
Grove expected to seek shareholder approval in the first quarter 1997, it said.
The newly expanded company would then reduce its quarterly fund flows from operations (FFO) payout ratio from about 76 percent to about 63 percent of FFO, Grove said.

Grove said it would use the retained cash flow to make acquisitions which would increase total return over the long-term. The company said the decreased payout ratio was not a response to any negative business or operational trend.

The company said its board also authorized the repurchase of up to 100,000 shares of Grove Property Trust, after the consolidation of properties. But Grove said there was no guarantee the consolidation would be completed.
